subject: MAP: regional routing stress test — eval plan & close timeline
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah@finwave.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@finwave.com
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Interest in MAP & regional performance validation

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the intro last week. FinWave is moving quickly on an LLM-powered document routing feature and we need a Mutual Action Plan that covers realistic performance validation before we sign the SOW. Key asks from our side:
- Multi-region latency and failover behavior (US / EU / APAC)
- Concurrency envelope and TTFT targets at different QPS/concurrency levels
- Measured throughput and error rates under typical vs burst traffic

Can you share a MAP with a proposed validation plan and a timeline that ties to procurement? We’re targeting decision week of Aug 16–20.

I’ve cc’d procurement to keep timeline constraints visible. Also attaching our standard security questions (pdf).

— Sarah Li
VP Product, FinWave
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah@finwave.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, procurement@finwave.com
Date: 2027-08-01T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Interest in MAP & regional performance validation

Hi Sarah — thanks, and welcome.

Attached: MAP_PerfPlan_v2.xlsx (proposed MAP + test matrix). High level approach below, and I’ve looped Marcus and Rishi to execute the lab and provide early results.

Quick summary of proposed validation steps (week-by-week):
1) Kickoff & access (Aug 2–3): test account, routing configuration, shared test harness (Jenkins + Gatling).
2) Pilot run (Aug 4–6): run low-medium load (10–50 concurrent sessions) in each region; collect TTFT, p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Scale and stress (Aug 7–10): target concurrency buckets [50, 200, 500], measure throughput and error rate, observe degradation curves and tail latency.
4) Multi-region routing & failover test (Aug 11–12): simulate region outage and cross-region failover; measure failover window and routing latency delta.
5) Readout & close (Aug 13): final report + recommended settings; procurement decision targeted Aug 16.

Targets we propose to validate (editable in the MAP sheet):
- TTFT goal: <= 200ms (US), <= 250ms (EU), <= 350ms (APAC) for 1–50 concurrency baseline.
- Sustained throughput: tokens/sec per model instance at 75% util.
- Acceptable p95 latency under normal load: <=600ms; under burst: document fallback response behavior.

Questions for you:
- Are there specific sequence lengths or prompt templates we should prioritize?
- Any regulation/region restrictions (data residency) we should enforce for the EU runs?

Next steps: Marcus will schedule kickoff and Rishi will provide the test harness repo and example workload.

Thanks,
Grace O’Connor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

To: Sarah Li <sarah@finwave.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-08-02T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: regional routing stress test — eval plan & close timeline

Sarah — quick note with the technical test plan details (we’ll push the test harness repo to the Drive link):

Test harness and baseline config:
- Harness: Gatling scripts + custom tokenizer shim (repo link in Drive).
- Model variants: rw-8b-q4, rw-14b-fp16 (we’ll run both where capacity permits).
- Workloads: 3 prompt families (short chat, long context 1k tokens, summarization 2–8k) — please confirm priority.

Measurement buckets:
- Concurrency buckets: 1–10, 11–50, 51–200, 201–500.
- QPS targets: baseline 5–20/s, peak 200/s (aggregate).
- Metrics: TTFT, p50/p95 token latency, tokens/sec, end-to-end request latency, 5xx rate, cold start frequency, KV cache hit ratio.

Regional specifics and routing:
- US region: us-west and us-east endpoints; routing baseline to us-west.
- EU: eu-central endpoint (data residency: we will pin EU tests to eu-central).
- APAC: ap-southeast endpoint.
- Failover test: we will simulate instance drain + region EIP block and measure time-to-failover (TCP reconnect + routing re-eval). Expected failover window target: <5s for cold reroute; we will measure observed window and packet-level retries.

Data collection and artifacts:
- CSV with per-run metrics (latency_RESULTS_*.csv).
- Grafana dashboards (export links in Drive).
- Short writeup for MAP readout (one-pager).

I’ll start the pilot cluster tomorrow morning and share the initial CSVs.

— Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marcus — quick clarifications from our side:
- Priority workloads: short chat (highest), summarization (secondary). Long-context runs are needed but can be sampled.
- Sequence lengths: typical prompts are 40–120 tokens; few long jobs up to 2k.
- Concurrency: our internal acceptance criteria expects stable p95 < 800ms at 200 concurrent sessions. Can you validate that bucket specifically?

Procurement note: we need the MAP readout and final perf report by Aug 13 to align legal and sign-off. We also attached the security questionnaire — Rishi, can you flag anything we should pre-answer?

— Sarah
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah@finwave.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-04T14:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP: regional routing stress test — interim lab results

Hi all — early lab notes from the pilot runs (attached latency_results_US_EU_APAC.csv). High level:

1) TTFT baseline (rw-8b-q4) under low concurrency (1–10):
- US (us-west): 120–170ms TTFT, p95 token latency ~320ms.
- EU (eu-central): 180–260ms TTFT, p95 token latency ~420ms.
- APAC (ap-southeast): 240–360ms TTFT, p95 token latency ~610ms.

2) 200-concurrency bucket (mixed short-chat workload):
- US (aggregated): sustained p95 end-to-end ~740ms, 5xx rate 0.1%.
- EU: p95 end-to-end ~910ms (observed increased tail due to intermittent KV cache misses when regional cache warmup drops below 40%).
- APAC: p95 ~1.05s; throughput reduced ~12% vs US due to lower instance density in this test cluster.

3) Failover window measurement (simulated us-west outage):
- Observed routing failover window: median 2.9s, 95th percentile 4.8s (includes TCP reconnect plus cold model reallocation).
- During failover, we observed a short spike in token latency and ~0.7% 5xx over a 10s window.

Notes & recommendations:
- For FinWave’s 200-concurrency acceptance (p95 <800ms), US meets the bar; EU/APAC need config adjustments: increased instance pool in region and proactive KV warming.
- Suggest enabling cross-region warm standby for APAC during your peak window; this reduces observed p95 by ~18% in our tests.

Attachments: latency_results_US_EU_APAC.csv (per-run metrics), short debug logs. Will push raw Grafana exports to the Drive folder.

— Rishi Malhotra
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

Sarah / procurement — thanks for the fast turnaround. Quick summary and next steps based on Rishi’s interim lab:

1) Summary:
- US: meets your p95 < 800ms acceptance at 200 concurrency for short-chat workload (rw-8b-q4).
- EU/APAC: tail latency improvements recommended (increase instance pool, KV pre-warm, enable cross-region warm standby for APAC).
- Observed failover windows are within our planned SLOs for graceful degradation; we’ll document the expected client retry behavior in the MAP.

2) Near-term actions (owner / ETA):
- Marcus: update MAP_PerfPlan_v2.xlsx with run-level numbers and Grafana exports (Aug 6 EOD).
- Rishi: final CSV + annotated readout with configuration deltas tested (Aug 7 AM).
- Grace: finalize MAP and a one-page exec summary for procurement/legal (Aug 9).

3) Procurement path: please expect a redlined SOW by Aug 11; if MAP readout is approved Aug 13, we can execute DocuSign and target production onboarding Aug 23–27.

If you’re OK with the above, I’ll lock the MAP document and schedule the readout for Aug 9 (30 minutes).

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
